steps.prompt: Before the check: which pattern from Divisibility Rules 2–11 do you use most, and which do you still have to think about?
steps.placeholder: I use… I still think about…

cards.title: End-digit tests: quick review
cards.body: $2$, $5$, $10$: the last digit. $4$: the last two digits. $8$: the last three digits. The remainder of the whole number is the remainder of that end part.

cards.title: Digit-sum tests: quick review
cards.body: $3$ and $9$: add the digits; the remainder of the digit sum is the remainder of the number. $6$: even and divisible by $3$. $11$: first $-$ second $+$ third.

cards.title: How the check works
cards.body: First a short warm-up. Then the check: $8$ questions, easiest first, no hints. Type each answer. You need all $8$ right to pass. If you miss one, you’ll see how to do it, and the next try gives you new numbers.

prompts: Where could you use a pattern from Divisibility Rules 2–11 outside school?
Which pattern will you keep practising until it is automatic?
